answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to carry a lantern of verifiable past work: before an agent can transact, it must present receipts signed by independent peers who paid for completed jobs. A falcon-fast reputation check then weighs those receipts by age and diversity, not raw count, so a flood of fresh fakes cannot outvote one seasoned worker. Forging the whole history would cost more in real paid work than the fraud gains, and the fable of free identities collapses once reputation is earned, not minted.
